If $d_2(E)\in\{0,1\}$, then $$a(E)=r(E)=c_2(E)=d_2(E),\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(E/\mathbb Q)\text{ is finite},\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(E/\mathbb Q)[2^\infty]=0.$$

For an elliptic curve $A/\mathbb Q$ there is an exact sequence $$0\longrightarrow A(\mathbb Q)\otimes\mathbb Q_2/\mathbb Z_2
 \longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{Sel}}_{2^\infty}(A/\mathbb Q)
 \longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(A/\mathbb Q)[2^\infty]\longrightarrow0.$$ In particular $$c_2(A)=r(A)+\mathop{\mathrm{corank}}_{\mathbb Z_2}\mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(A/\mathbb Q)[2^\infty].$$ If $a(A)\le1$, then $r(A)=a(A)$, the whole group $\mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(A/\mathbb Q)$ is finite, and $c_2(A)=a(A)$.

For every elliptic curve $A/\mathbb Q$ with root number $\varepsilon(A)$, $$(-1)^{c_2(A)}=\varepsilon(A).$$ A rational isogeny preserves $a(A)$, $r(A)$ and $c_2(A)$. For a quadratic field $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{k})$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{corank}}_{\mathbb Z_2}\mathop{\mathrm{Sel}}_{2^\infty}(A/K) =c_2(A)+c_2(A^{(k)}).$$

The representation $E[2]$ is reducible over $\mathbb F_2$ if and only if $E(\mathbb Q)[2]\ne0$. In that case it is an extension of two trivial $\mathbb F_2$-representations. Otherwise its image is $C_3$ or $S_3$ in $\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_2(\mathbb F_2)$. Quadratic twisting leaves this representation unchanged.

Let $F$ be the quotient of $\mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(E/\mathbb Q)[2^\infty]$ by its maximal divisible subgroup. Then $$d_2(E)=c_2(E)+\dim_{\mathbb F_2}F[2],
 \qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_2}F[2]\text{ is even}.$$ Thus $d_2(E)\in\{0,1\}$ implies $c_2(E)=d_2(E)$ and $F=0$.

 2j(P_{|h_x|}(h_x))-4w(h_x)-s(h_x)-s(h_xk)\le B.$$ Then, for sufficiently large $b$, the base product has a simple zero. The dimension threshold depends only on the fixed base and the displayed bounds, not on the number or sizes of the new primes. The field $K$ may vary with the family.

 v(\mathcal L(h))\ge 2w(h)+s(h)-C_E.$$ The constant is independent of the number and sizes of the primes that divide $h$.

Let $E/\mathbb Q$ have conductor $N$, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes containing the prime divisors of $2N$. Prescribe a real sign $\sigma\in\{1,-1\}$ and a unit squareclass $c_p\in\mathbb Z_p^\times/\mathbb Z_p^{\times2}$ for each $p\in S$. Suppose that these data are realized by an odd fundamental discriminant, and that twists in this filter have root number $\varepsilon$. There are a holomorphic weight-$3/2$ cusp form $$g=\sum_{n\geq1}a(n)q^n$$ of level supported on $S$, after enlarging exponents at those primes, and finite-order characters $\psi,\eta$ of $2$-power order, with $\psi/\eta$ quadratic, having the following properties.* 1. *The coefficients vanish off the filter and, for $p\notin S$, $$a(p^2n)=\bigl(\eta(p)a_p(E)-\psi(p)(-n/p)\bigr)a(n) -p\eta(p)^2a(n/p^2). \label{cs:hecke-recurrence}$$ As usual a coefficient with a nonintegral index is zero.* 2. *After normalizing at one nonzero squarefree index, every squarefree coefficient in the filter is a rational number times a root of unity of $2$-power order. In particular $\ell\equiv-1\pmod{2^M}$.* 2. *After a fixed harmless decrease in the working precision, the forms satisfy Equation [cs:hecke-recurrence] modulo that precision, with characters $\eta_M,\psi_M$ of $2$-power order and quadratic ratio. Their squarefree coefficients have the form of a $2$-power phase times an integer modulo $2^M$.* 3. *If a coefficient is visible, meaning $v(a_M(D))13. Let $A_1(x),\ldots,A_q(x)\in\mathbb Z_2$ each be one specified Laurent coefficient of the evaluation of an element of $O[G]$. If $$b>q(2^{M-1}-1),$$ there is $x\ne0$ such that $A_i(x)\equiv A_i(0)\pmod{2^M}$ for every $i$.

Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be an Artin local ring, and let $D$ be a complex of flat $A$-modules. Suppose $H^*(D\otimes_A k)$ is finite dimensional and supported in $[a,b]$. There is a bounded finite free complex $C$, with $$\operatorname{rank}_A C^j=\dim_k H^j(D\otimes_A k),$$ and a strong deformation retraction $$i:C\longrightarrow D,\qquad p:D\longrightarrow C,\qquad pi=1,\qquad 1-ip=dh+hd.$$ Thus maps to the original complex, as well as maps between finite models, are available. Any fixed finite collection of chain maps, homotopies, triangles, and perfect pairings can be transported to these models.

The complex in Equation [eq:cy:positive-complex] is perfect over $R$ and computes derived coefficient specializations. There is a class $a\in H^1(C_S^+(\mathbb T))$ whose rational span is the real-place summand. Its integral index in that summand depends only on $E$ and the fixed real sign.

For every binary family and its ramification set $S$, the corrected class $z_S$ satisfies the central reciprocity formula [eq:cy:reciprocity-center] and the rational divisibility [eq:cy:divisibility]. For some $c_E\ge0$ depending only on $E$, $$2^{c_E}z_S\in H^1\!\left(C_S(\mathbb T)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O[G]\right).$$ The same exponent works for all $S$, binary families, and fixed factors $h_0$ with the specified local classes. Here the displayed cohomology is derived scalar extension of the Iwasawa complex.

There is a constant $C_{\mathrm{loc}}$, depending only on the fixed curve and local classes, with the following property. Suppose $c_2(E^{(h_x)})=0$. If $L(E^{(h_x)},1)=0$, then $u_x(0)=0$; if $L(E^{(h_x)},1)\ne0$, then $$\label{eq:cy:determinant-center}
 \bigl|v_2(u_x(0))-D(h_x)\bigr|\leq C_{\mathrm{loc}}.$$ The rational positive complex at $t=0$ has cohomology only in degree one, of dimension two, so these are specializations of the same determinant.

If $E[2]$ is an extension of two trivial $\mathbb F_2$-modules, then there is an isomorphism in the derived category $$C_S^+(\mathbb T)\otimes_R\mathcal O[G]
       \simeq \mathcal O[G]^2[-1].$$

Suppose that $q$ is an added prime and $v_2(q^2-1)\le L$. At augmentation $G\to1$, the inverse singular Frobenius block contributed by $q$ has, modulo each fixed $2^M$, negative Laurent support bounded in terms of $L$ and $M$. This bound is independent of $q$.

Suppose diagrams of bounded finite free complexes over $A_i$, or over $A_i[G]$, have a common bounded cohomological degree interval and bounded ranks in every degree. Include the chain homotopies and inverses for every asserted identity or equivalence. Along a cofinal subsequence, or a nonprincipal ultrafilter, their matrices converge to the same diagram of perfect complexes over $\Lambda$ or $\Lambda[G]$.* *Moreover, the contractions into the original cochains may be retained for the evaluation construction in Lemma [rl:evaluation]. Adding finitely many new objects or maps does not require changing already chosen models for the old objects. Finite-stage arithmetic operations with unbounded source complexes are permitted when only finitely many of their outputs, and the witnesses to their identities, are retained in the bounded target complexes.

Let $F$ be a finite extension of a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, and let $B/F$ be any elliptic curve. Put $M_F=B(F)^\wedge_2=\varprojlim_n B(F)/2^nB(F)$. There is a perfect local condition $$U_F=M_F[-1]\longrightarrow R\Gamma(F,T_2B).$$ For every $n\geq1$, derived reduction has $$H^0(U_F\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathbf Z/2^n)=B(F)[2^n],\qquad H^1(U_F\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathbf Z/2^n)=B(F)/2^nB(F).$$ Its map in degree zero is the isomorphism onto $H^0(F,B[2^n])$, and its map in degree one is the finite Kummer injection. The condition is its own exact orthogonal complement under local Tate duality, for every reduction type and with no hypothesis on $B[2]$.

Fix finitely many split primes of $K$ above odd rational primes, outside $2N$, and orient one prime in each conjugate pair. There are distinct split rational primes $r_i$ avoiding all the fixed data and characters $$\xi_i:\operatorname{Gal}(H_{r_i}/K)\longrightarrow \mathbf Z/2^{n_i}\mathbf Z, \qquad n_i\longrightarrow\infty,$$ such that $\xi_i$ is surjective on the inertia quotient at $r_i$, is zero at the primes above $2N$, and has odd value at each prescribed oriented prime. We can require $r_i\to1$ in $\mathbf Z_2$ and $$\label{eq:h:r-avoidance} v_2(2+a_{r_i}(E)),\quad v_2(2-a_{r_i}(E)),\quad v_2\det(1\pm\operatorname{Fr}_{r_i}\mid T)\ \leq c_E.$$ The constant $c_E$ is independent of the list and of $K$.

For a primitive character constituent, let $C$ denote the limiting Selmer complex with full conditions at $r$ and at its active good conductor primes, and the prescribed Kummer, unramified or derivative conditions elsewhere. The limiting full local complexes are acyclic over every height-one residue field of $\Lambda$ of characteristic zero. At $(2)$, with residue field $\Omega=\mathbf F_2((t))$, the $r$-complex is acyclic, as are the complexes at active split primes with odd prescribed Frobenius exponent of the deformation character and at active primes $q$ with $t_q=0$. At each of these acyclic relaxed places, the full and orthogonal strict conditions agree on the indicated test. If every relaxed place is acyclic at that test and the remaining local conditions are self-dual, global duality makes the Selmer complex self-dual. The Selmer complex has no global invariants on these tests.

For a simple-zero instance, $$\label{eq:h:central-determinant}
 \begin{aligned}
 v(u(0))&=2j(P_c(e))
   -\mathop{\mathrm{length}}\mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(E^{(e)}/K)[2^\infty]
   -\sum_{q\mid c}\sum_{v\mid q}t_v+O_E(1),\\
 t_v&=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}E[2]^{\mathop{\mathrm{Fr}}_v}.
 \end{aligned}$$ Furthermore, $$\label{eq:h:weil-restriction-length}
 \mathop{\mathrm{length}}\mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(E^{(e)}/K)[2^\infty]
       +\sum_{q\mid c}\sum_{v\mid q}t_v
 =s(e)+s(ek)+\sum_{q\mid k}t_q
                         +2\sum_{q\mid c}t_q+O_E(1).$$ The constants include the one fixed class multiplier and the bounded local contribution at the moving prime $r_i$.

Fix $K$ and a sequence of the finite cochain constructions above. Keep the contraction maps into the original global cochains. Let $\Gamma_K=\prod_i G_K$ and $\Gamma=\Gamma_K\rtimes\langle\tau\rangle\subset\prod_iG_{\mathbf Q}$, with simultaneous complex conjugation $\tau$. Thus $\Gamma_K$ has index two in $\Gamma$; the larger unrestricted product of rational Galois groups is not used for induction. The matrix limit defines a coefficient action of $\Gamma_K$ on $\Lambda^2$. For every field $L$ receiving a map from $\Lambda$, there is a natural injection $$H^1(C\otimes_\Lambda L)\longrightarrow H^1_{\rm abs}(\Gamma_K,L^2),$$ where the right side denotes abstract crossed-homomorphism classes. Here $C$ may be the global complex or a Selmer complex whose local conditions contain all local degree-zero invariants and inject into local $H^1$. The same statement holds for the induced representation of $\Gamma$.* *The evaluation maps and their degree-two cochain identities exist for every group sequence and commute with coefficient extension.

In the notation of Lemma [rl:evaluation], let $H$ be the group of sequences each of whose entries acts trivially on the full Tate module, on all ring-class fields of $K$, and on the quadratic characters in use. Restriction from the crossed classes in that Lemma to $H$ is injective at every characteristic-zero test. It is also injective at the residual $(2)$ test. The characteristic-zero annihilator needed for this assertion can be chosen with a fixed finite $2$-valuation depending only on $E$, also as $K$ varies.

On an inner characteristic-zero test where $\Psi^2\ne1$, the four-dimensional representation induced from $T\chi\Psi$ is absolutely irreducible. If $\Psi^2=1$ on an inner test, it splits as two inequivalent absolutely irreducible quadratic twists.

For any element $u$ of an exact kernel in Lemma 81, derivative primes can be chosen, at increasing finite precision, whose rational Frobenius is $\tau u$ on all retained data. Their finite localization is evaluation on $(\tau u)^2$. The assertion is compatible with any fixed finite list of previous derivative operations.

Let a sequence of inert good primes $\ell$ have rational Frobenius lifts tending on $T$ to a fixed complex conjugation $C_\tau$. At the unique prime of $K$ above $\ell$, the limiting local complex has $$H^0=M,\qquad H^1=F\oplus S=M\oplus M,\qquad H^2=M, \label{rd:local-cohomology}$$ with zero differentials in a free split model. Here $M=T\otimes\Lambda$ with the relevant scalar coefficient structure. The two degree-one coordinates of a cocycle are $$f(c)=c(\gamma^2),\qquad s(c)=c(\sigma), \label{eq:h:local-coordinates}$$ where $\sigma$ is an oriented pro-$2$ tame generator. The plane conditions $F=\{s=0\}$ and $S=\{f=0\}$ include $H^0$ and exclude $H^2$. Each is its own orthogonal complement for conjugate-Weil duality. The strict condition $H^0$ and the relaxed condition $H^0\oplus H^1[-1]$ are mutually dual. All four inclusions can be equipped with compatible integral duality triangles.

Suppose that the finite ring-class transfers are performed before retaining their target cycles and witnesses as in Lemma 74. There is one integer $L\ne0$, depending on the fixed curve, parametrization and fixed local types, such that the classes obtained from the Heegner derivatives of $L$ times the point satisfy, for every finite switched set $I$, $$P_I\in H^1(C_I),\qquad f(P_{I\cup\{\ell\}})=0,\qquad s(P_{I\cup\{\ell\}})=C_\tau f(P_I). \label{eq:h:finite-singular}$$ The same $L$ works for every number of active and derivative primes. The previously imposed singular conditions are retained.

Let $\mathcal O$ be a height-one discrete valuation ring at which the complexes and switching conditions are self-dual. Suppose the generic Selmer group for a set $I$ has rank one and is spanned by $P_I$, and $v_0=f(P_I)$ is nonzero at the next derivative prime. Then the switched generic group has rank one and is spanned by $P_{I\cup\{l\}}$, and $$\label{eq:h:switch-equality}
 v_{\mathcal O}(u_I)=v_{\mathcal O}(u_{I\cup\{l\}}).$$ This assertion does not require a primitive localization in either integral plane.

Suppose a primitive instance has generic cohomology of rank at most one in degrees one and two, zero elsewhere, and $P$ spans $H^1$ when it is nonzero. Then the first line of Equation [eq:h:divisor-bounds] holds. These hypotheses hold in every simple-zero instance and also at the base of Theorem 10. The second line holds in genus data with irreducible $E[2]$, with a bound independent of the number of active or derivative primes.

Suppose $\omega(\operatorname{disc}K)\leq A$, the local twisting classes at $2N$ belong to a fixed finite list, and all active conductor primes are split with odd Frobenius exponent of the deformation character. After localization and completion at $(2)$, the minimal free ranks of the Selmer complexes are bounded in terms of $E,A$, and the number of retained derivative primes. They do not depend on the number of active conductor primes.

Let $C_j$ be any family of the preceding limiting complexes, completed over $\mathcal O_j=\widehat{\Lambda_{(2)}}$, possibly for different quadratic fields $K_j$. Suppose their minimal ranks are bounded. Assume a common bounded cohomological degree interval. Keep the actual evaluation matrices and transport them to the minimal models through integral contractions. For a nonprincipal ultrafilter $\mathcal U$, put $$\mathcal O_\infty=
 \left(\prod_{\mathcal U}\mathcal O_j\right)/\mathfrak a,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak a=\{(x_j):
    \{j:v_2(x_j)\geq n\}\in\mathcal U\text{ for every }n\}.$$ Then $\mathcal O_\infty$ is a DVR with uniformizer $2$ and a characteristic-zero fraction field $L_\infty$. The outer $H^1$ over $L_\infty$ injects into crossed classes on the inner quadratic sequence group product, or its extension by one simultaneous complex conjugation for the induced representation. Its restriction to the product of their exact common kernels is injective. All arbitrary-sequence degree-two evaluation identities survive. These conclusions also hold after retaining any fixed finite collection of additional integral diagrams.
On the outer characteristic-zero test, $\Psi$ has infinite order and the four-dimensional representation induced from $T\chi\Psi$ is absolutely irreducible.
The finite Chebotarev realization of Lemma 83 is compatible with Proposition 89 and with any fixed finite list of previous derivative operations.

The finite free models, ring-class characters, local conditions and pairings constructed above can be retained simultaneously. Their inner limits have the stated height-one acyclicity and all-sequence cohomology detection. For all-split ring data with bounded $\omega(\operatorname{disc}K)$, the residual model sizes are bounded independently of the active conductor support. Their outer limits retain arbitrary evaluations, exact-kernel injectivity and finite Chebotarev realization after any fixed number of additional integral arithmetic operations.

For simple-zero ring data with every active conductor prime split in $K$ and $\omega(k)\le a$, the coordinate of Definition 78 satisfies $$v_{(2)}(u)\ge -C_{E,a},$$ where $C_{E,a}$ is independent of $h$ and $K$. There is no residual irreducibility assumption. This is the last line of Equation [eq:h:divisor-bounds].

There is $\eta\in O[G]$ such that $u=\eta u_{\mathrm{rel}}$ agrees at each character with the primitive determinant coordinate up to a $\Lambda$-unit. In particular, $u_x\in\Lambda[1/2]$. If the base product derivative is zero, then $u_0(0)=0$. At the nonzero vertices, $$\label{eq:h:normalized-vertex-bound}
 v(u_x(0))\le B+O_{E,h_0,a}(1),$$ where $a$ bounds $\omega(k)$.

For the element $u$ of Lemma 94, there are $f,d\in O[G]$ with $d_x=f_xu_x$ at every character, $f_0\in\Lambda$, and $v(f_0(0))$ uniformly bounded. For each fixed $M$, the negative Laurent support of every $f_x\bmod2^M$ has a bound independent of $b$ and of the number of new primes.

coverage.oracle_basis: The oracle counts the returned maps and compares the count with the input dimension. It verifies every map's shape and binary entries before reconstructing its pullback.
